cards.text: The apostle Peter is writing to believers, and he calls them beloved. He also calls them foreigners and exiles, and friend, I KNOW that feeling. YEARS in a junk drawer, trying to fit in next to a takeout menu.

cards.question: Peter urges these beloved foreigners and exiles to stay away from something that wars against their soul. What is it?

cards.text: Here's what these believers are up against. The Gentiles around them slander them as evildoers, like they're the villain in somebody else's group chat.

cards.question: Peter tells the believers to answer the Gentiles who slander them by slandering them right back.
Peter wants the believers to live with such honor that the people slandering them see their good deeds and ___ God on the day He visits us.

cards.text: Next, Peter tells them to submit to every human institution, from the king as the supreme authority to the governors he sends. I already submit to my oven timer, friend, and that thing is the SUPREME authority in my bakery.

cards.question: Peter tells the believers to submit themselves to every human institution for the ___'s sake.
Peter says the king sends governors. What are those governors sent to do?

answers.text: Guard the borders of the land

cards.text: Peter says it's God's will that the ignorance of foolish men gets silenced, and it won't be with a clever comeback. Good thing, because it once took me THREE DAYS in that drawer to think of a comeback for a rubber band.

cards.question: So how does God want the believers to silence the ignorance of foolish men?

cards.text: Then Peter tells them, "Live in freedom." Friend, after all those years in a drawer, nobody has to tell ME twice.

cards.question: Peter warns the believers never to use their freedom as a cover-up for evil.
Instead of using their freedom for evil, Peter tells the believers to live as ___ of God.

cards.text: Then Peter gives them one short line, starting with this: treat everyone with high regard. Three quick commands follow, and I'd have to write them on my apron just to remember them.

cards.question: In that short line, Peter says to love the brotherhood of believers and to fear God. Who does he say to honor?

cards.text: Now Peter speaks to servants. He tells them to submit to their masters with all respect.

cards.question: Which masters does Peter tell servants to submit to?

answers.text: Only the good and gentle ones

cards.text: Then Peter talks about enduring the pain of unjust suffering. That's the kind of pain nobody earned.

cards.question: Peter says that when someone endures unjust pain because he is conscious of God, this is to be commended.

cards.text: Then Peter compares two people who both suffer and both endure it. Same gritted teeth, friend. VERY different performance review.

cards.question: Peter says that if you suffer for doing ___ and you endure it, this is commendable before God.

cards.text: Peter says this is what they were called to. Why? Because Christ also suffered for them.

cards.question: When Christ suffered for them, what did He leave behind so they could follow in His footsteps?
Peter quotes Scripture saying Jesus committed no sin and no deceit was found in His mouth.

cards.text: Now Peter shows what that example looked like when people heaped abuse on Jesus.

cards.question: When people heaped abuse on Jesus and He suffered, He paid them back with threats.
Instead of making threats when He suffered, who did Jesus entrust Himself to?

answers.text: The friends who stood by Him

cards.text: Then Peter goes deeper. Jesus Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree.

cards.question: Peter says Jesus bore our sins so that we might ___ to sin and ___ to righteousness.

cards.text: Then Peter quotes Scripture: "By His stripes you are healed."
Then Peter says they were like sheep going astray. Friend, I go astray walking from my oven to the sprinkles, and I live on a planet just big enough for a bakery.

cards.question: But now, Peter says, those wandering sheep have returned. Who have they returned to?

answers.text: The Shepherd and Overseer of their souls
The king and the governors he sends
The elders of their own towns

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "Live in freedom.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card calls Peter 'the apostle Peter', but that fact comes from outside the passage (1 Peter 1:1). The card cites only 1 Peter 2:11 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new drawer event: it took Papa Dorin three days to think of a comeback for a rubber band. The docs let jokes make up small moments around his bakery, but they don't say whether jokes can make up new moments from his junk-drawer years.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes make up small new moments from his time in the junk drawer, like a comeback for a rubber band, or only moments around his bakery?

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only', so the right answer is the odd one out. A baker can spot it from the wording without knowing the verse.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card says Peter 'quotes Scripture' but never says which Scripture. That is a fact from outside the passage (Isaiah 53:9), and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The One who judges fairly', uses a capitalized 'One' and sounds like it's about God. The wrong answers ('The friends who stood by Him', 'The crowds who followed Him') don't sound that way, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says Peter 'quotes Scripture' ('By His stripes you are healed') but never says which Scripture. The source is Isaiah 53:5, and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only 1 Peter 2:24.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in this stop are flat restatements with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice (cards 1, 7, 10, 13, 15). Holding back jokes around Christ's suffering is right, but his warmth and storyteller voice can still come through. Card 1 especially reads like a plain summary.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
